title: Difficulty breathing / not breathing
content: If a pet is not breathing, gasping, or showing severe difficulty breathing, this is a life-threatening emergency. Call the clinic's emergency line immediately or go directly to the nearest emergency vet — do not wait for an online response.

title: Severe bleeding
content: Heavy or uncontrolled bleeding from a wound is an emergency. Apply gentle pressure with a clean cloth if possible and come to the clinic immediately or call the emergency line.

title: Suspected poisoning
content: If your pet may have eaten something toxic (chocolate, rat poison, human medication, certain plants), this is an emergency. Do not induce vomiting unless instructed by a vet. Call the emergency line immediately and bring the packaging of the suspected substance if possible.

title: Unconscious or unresponsive pet
content: An unconscious or unresponsive pet is a critical emergency. Go to the nearest emergency vet or call the clinic's 24/7 emergency line right away.

title: Insect or snake bite / sting
content: Bites or stings that cause swelling, difficulty breathing, or sudden weakness are emergencies. Call the emergency line immediately.

title: Mild vomiting once
content: A single episode of vomiting with a pet that is otherwise alert and active is usually not an emergency, but should be monitored. If vomiting continues, contains blood, or the pet seems lethargic, book a same-day appointment or call the clinic.
